title: Sleep ladder
header: HERE IS WHAT YOUR **SLEEP** DOES TO YOUR FACE

S8.base: woman, age 29, hair tied back, no make-up, neutral expression, normal rested skin, grey crew neck

S9.edit: face only: skin slightly brighter and more even, eyes a touch more open

S6.edit: face only: faint shadows under both eyes, skin slightly duller

S5.edit: face only: darker under-eye circles, mild puffiness of the lower lids, skin dull

S4.edit: face only: very tired look after a sleepless night, dark circles under the eyes, puffy lower eyelids, heavy drooping upper eyelids, lips a little paler, dull complexion

beats.vo: Here is what your sleep does to your face, starting with nine full hours in bed.
Eight hours is her baseline, the face she wakes up with after a completely normal night.
At six hours, the first grey shadows settle in under both eyes and the skin dulls.
Five hours, and the lower lids start to swell while the skin loses its healthy colour.
At four hours the upper lids hang, the lips go pale and the whole face greys.
In one study, the same people looked less healthy and less attractive when sleep deprived.
Another study found hanging lids, swollen eyes and darker circles after one missed night of sleep.
None of this is bone, and every step of it comes back with sleep.
Comment how many hours you got last night.
